findings.issue: English gloss for ネックレス is 'to glue, to paste' — that is a translation of the Portuguese homograph 'colar' (verb), not of the Japanese word. ネックレス means 'necklace' (noun), as the pt gloss and the sentence context show.

何か in 何かありますか is read なにか; なんか is a colloquial contraction that clashes with the polite ありますか register and is not the standard reading. The romaji 'nanka' inherits the same error (should be 'nanika').
findings.current: かばんのなかになんかありますか
findings.suggested: かばんのなかになにかありますか

findings.issue: Reading of 何 (part of 何か 'something') is given as なん; in the pronoun 何か the standard reading is なに (なにか).

Learner-facing explanation apologizes for an internal tokenizer error instead of the data being fixed: tokens つまら+ない should be merged into a single token つまらない. Same remark appears in expl_pt ('o tokenizador o dividiu por engano').
findings.current: Note that つまらない is a single い-adjective (boring/dull); the tokenizer wrongly split it into つまら+ない.
findings.suggested: (delete this sentence in expl_en and expl_pt; merge tokens つまら+ない into one token つまらない, r=つまらない)

findings.issue: Learner-facing explanation apologizes for a parser error instead of the tokens being fixed: つか+れ should be one token つかれ (疲れ, te-form stem of 疲れる). Same remark appears in expl_pt ('o analisador automático separou ... em pedaços errados').
findings.current: Note: the automatic parser split つかれている into the wrong pieces; it is a single verb, 疲れる.
findings.suggested: (delete this note in expl_en and expl_pt; retokenize つか+れ as one token つかれ (疲れ), followed by て+いる)

findings.issue: 'As for Grandma' renders subject-marker が as if it were topic は, contradicting the item's own expl_en, which correctly teaches that が marks the doer. The topic device should be reserved for は; here the literal mirror misrepresents the structure.
findings.current: As for Grandma, she gave me sweets.

findings.issue: 'Quanto à vovó' apresenta が como se fosse o tópico は, contradizendo a própria expl_pt do item (が marca quem realiza a ação). O espelho literal ensina uma estrutura que não está na frase.
findings.current: Quanto à vovó, (ela) deu doces (a mim).
findings.suggested: A vovó (sujeito が) deu doces (a mim).

findings.issue: The natural-translation field is an infinitive fragment (reads like a dictionary definition), while the natural full sentence ended up in lit_en instead. en should be a finite sentence.
findings.current: To be wearing a necklace around your neck.
findings.suggested: I'm wearing a necklace around my neck.

findings.issue: Mesmo problema do en: tradução natural em infinitivo, sem sujeito finito, soando como verbete de dicionário em vez de frase.
findings.current: Estar usando um colar no pescoço.
findings.suggested: Estou usando um colar no pescoço.
